name: Arizona Biological and Biomedical Sciences (ABBS)

sources.label: University of Arizona ABBS: How to apply
University of Arizona Graduate College: English proficiency

summary: An umbrella first-year program for biology and biomedical PhD students at the University of Arizona. Students rotate through labs, then join one of the participating programs; admitted students are funded.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: Page: 'The application portal for Fall 2027 is open from September 1, 2026 - December 1, 2026.' All materials, including letters of reference, are due December 1, 2026. No time or time zone is stated.

timeline.interviews: Applicants chosen for interviews are notified starting in mid-December and attend a recruitment session; the admission process runs early December through mid-March. Virtual interviews are offered to applicants outside the US. (The FAQ still names Fall 2025 interview weekends, so check the current dates.)

english.note: University of Arizona Graduate College minimums for international applicants: IELTS composite 7 with no subject area below 6; Pearson PTE Academic 60 also accepted. Individual departments may require higher scores. Exemptions apply for applicants whose native language is English or with two years of full-time study in the US or English-speaking Canada.

applicationFee.note: The FAQ says 'The ABBS program is not able to provide any fee waivers, regardless of financial or citizenship status.'

documents: Unofficial transcripts of all college and university work
requirements.note: At least one letter should come from a research advisor or supervisor. Recommenders must respond by the December 1 deadline.

funding.note: All incoming students, regardless of citizenship status, are offered a $32,500 yearly stipend (the FAQ gives no year), tuition and health insurance; funding is guaranteed for the next 4-5 years in the lab and program joined, with satisfactory progress.
